visual.general_description: Two horizontally arranged panels showing clinical overview A and dermoscopy B.
visual.detailed_description: Panel A shows a small round pale-pink lesion amid light-brown scalp hair; panel B gives a magnified view with intersecting hair shafts, central pink region and faint fine reddish lines. Printed letters A/B identify panels. No scale or numeric measurement appears.

panels.general_description: Overview photograph of a small round lesion in a hair-covered scalp.
panels.detailed_description: Left panel A is a clinical color photograph with tan/pink skin and numerous light-brown hair shafts swept toward the upper-right corner, where a small shiny metal hair clip is visible. A small round pale pink/translucent-looking raised region lies beside the hair part, with a lighter edge and nearby fine hairs. White label A sits at bottom left. There is no ruler, arrow or printed size. The lesion occupies a small area of the overall photograph.

evidence.quote: The lesion was diagnosed as a membranous variant of ACC, and a conservative approach with regular clinical follow-up was adopted.
Scalp solitary bullous lesion filled with clear liquid.

limitations: No scale is shown; clinical 5 mm and ultrasound 5×15 mm dimensions are article measurements and cannot be measured from this image.
Clear fluid, named vascular/follicular structures and diagnosis are author-supported claims; visual inspection does not establish tissue histology or deeper bone involvement.

panels.general_description: Dermoscopy close-up of the same author-identified lesion.
panels.detailed_description: Right panel B is a magnified color view with many long dark-brown hair shafts crossing a pale pink/white field. A central rounded pink/translucent-looking region has a pale surrounding rim; faint fine reddish lines are visible within it. Several short dark oval/linear elements occur along its lower/lateral margin among the hairs. White label B sits at bottom left. No scale, magnification number, arrow or measurement is printed. Individual fine structures overlap with hair shafts.

evidence.quote: B) Dermoscopy shows fine arborizing vessels over a translucent background within which is possible to observe hair roots and hair bulbs arranged in an arch shape along the margins of the lesion.
The lesion was diagnosed as a membranous variant of ACC, and a conservative approach with regular clinical follow-up was adopted.

assignments.subject: patient

evidence.quote: Physical examination revealed a 5 mm bullous lesion on the right parasagittal scalp region (Figure 1A).

Dermoscopy demonstrated fine arborizing vessels overlying a translucent background, allowing visualization of hair roots and bulbs aligned in an archlike distribution at the periphery of the lesion (Figure 1B).

assignments.rationale: Sole original case explicitly links physical examination to 1A and dermoscopy to 1B; no identity inferred from appearance.
